newsitem.title: USA: MEAT--USDA sees export report similar to grains.
newsitem.headline: MEAT--USDA sees export report similar to grains.

text.p: USDA envisions its proposed meat export sales rules will be similar to those currently in place for grains and oilseeds, a USDA document said.
"Reporting would include quantity sold to foreign buyers, marketing year of shipment and country of destination," a Foreign Agriculture Service leaflet obtained by Reuters said.
Reporting would also include any changes in previously reported information, such as cancellations and destination changes, the leaflet said.
It said USDA foresaw that the reporting week would be Friday through Thursday, the same as for grains.

The proposal to require meat exporters to report sales activity is aimed at increasing information in the livestock markets and stems from recommendations by USDA's advisory committee on concentration in Agriculture.
USDA has drawn up an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on meat export reporting, which is currently awaiting approval by the White House's Office of Management and Budget.
USDA officials have said they expect the notice to be published in the next week or shortly thereafter.
The notice will call for public comments on whether reporting should be in pounds or tonnes, and whether actual weight or carcass weight should be reported, the leaflet said.

It will also call for comments on which meats should be considered -- suggesting beef, veal, pork, lamb, chicken and turkey -- and whether exporters should report whether the product is chilled or frozen.
The notice will also ask for public comment on what level of detail should be reported, the leaflet said.
The advisory committee on concentration had recommended that reporting be broken down by cuts and USDA grade, and that it should include variety meats and processed meats.
However, a USDA official said detailed reporting on individual cuts may present some logistical difficulties both for USDA and for exporters.

The leaflet made no mention of any proposal to require exporters to report export prices, which was one of the recommendations of the advisory committee. There are no price reporting requirements for grain exporters.
